Bug_Details:
Don't create instances of already existing BigInteger (`BigInteger.ZERO`, `BigInteger.ONE`),
for Java 1.5 onwards, BigInteger.TEN and BigDecimal (`BigDecimal.ZERO`, `BigDecimal.ONE`, `BigDecimal.TEN`) and
for Java 9 onwards `BigInteger.TWO`.
Examples:
BigInteger bi1 = new BigInteger("1");    // reference BigInteger.ONE instead
BigInteger bi2 = new BigInteger("0");    // reference BigInteger.ZERO instead
BigInteger bi3;
bi3 = new BigInteger("0");               // reference BigInteger.ZERO instead

BigDecimal bd1 = new BigDecimal(0);      // reference BigDecimal.ZERO instead
BigDecimal bd2 = new BigDecimal("0.") ;  // reference BigDecimal.ZERO instead
BigDecimal bd3 = new BigDecimal(10);     // reference BigDecimal.TEN instead
Bug_Explanation: The code demonstrates the improper instantiation of BigInteger and BigDecimal objects that have predefined constants available. Instead of using the constants BigInteger.ONE, BigInteger.ZERO, BigDecimal.ZERO, and BigDecimal.TEN, new instances are being created unnecessarily.
Trigger_Explanation: The test cases fail because they compare the improperly instantiated BigInteger and BigDecimal objects with their constant equivalents. Due to the bug, new instances are created instead of using the existing constants, causing the assertions to fail and thereby triggering the bug.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate that all tests passed successfully without any errors or failures, suggesting that the bug was not triggered during the test execution.
